stemMd: Which consumer behaviour is compatible with the cooperative's argument?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Replacing an appliance while still preferring products that last longer

options.label: B
options.textMd: Refusing to consider any cost information

options.label: C
options.textMd: Knowing nothing about whether an appliance is broken

options.label: D
options.textMd: Buying a replacement proves indifference to durability

options.label: E
options.textMd: Always choosing novelty when repair is free

explanationMd: A consumer may value durability yet replace a broken product when repair is prohibitively costly. Preferences must be interpreted within available options and constraints.

distractorRationale.b: The argument depends on practical costs.
distractorRationale.d: This is the inference being challenged.
distractorRationale.e: That would support the manufacturer's interpretation more directly.
distractorRationale.c: The case concerns response to failure.
